title: Practice 6: Perfective or imperfective? The prefixed verbs in use

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: I spent my vacation in Hakone.
exercises.why: **провел** is the past tense (masculine) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я хорошо провёл время.» (I had a good time.) — DLI, Lesson 79. «Мы провели в Европе два месяца.» (We spent two months in Europe.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choice: **проводил** is imperfective (**проводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **подлетал** is the past tense (masculine) of **подлетать** (to fly up (to), to approach; (colloquial) to run/rush up (to)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **подлететь**. past: он подлета́л · она подлета́ла · оно подлета́ло · они подлета́ли. — Wiktionary, «подлетать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. Antonym: от- Example: Он подошёл к девушке, чтобы спросить её номер. — He approached the girl to ask for her number. Prepositional phrases: к + dat.; до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **подлетел** is perfective (**подлететь**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He came in fifth in the race.
exercises.why: **пришел** is the past tense (masculine) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда?» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приходил** is imperfective (**приходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Tom raised his glass to his lips.
exercises.why: **поднёс** is the past tense (masculine) of **поднести** (to bring, to carry (to); to offer, to present) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **подносить**. past: он поднёс · она поднесла́ · оно поднесло́ · они поднесли́. — Wiktionary, «поднести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. Antonym: от- Example: Он подошёл к девушке, чтобы спросить её номер. — He approached the girl to ask for her number. Prepositional phrases: к + dat.; до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **подносил** is imperfective (**подносить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **пришла** is the past tense (feminine) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note. — The verbs приходить and приезжать usually refer to the habitual or repeated actions: Он приходит (приезжает) сюда каждый день. — He comes here every day. These verbs, as the other verbs of motion, may be used to express a single action in the future: Он приходит на работу завтра утром. — He is coming to work tomorrow morning. Она приезжает из Москвы сегодня вечером. — She is coming (arriving) from Moscow this evening. When the action is in progress in the present such expressions as "He is coming" or "He is on the way here" are expressed in Russian in the following way: Кто это идёт (едет) сюда?» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choice: **приходила** is imperfective (**приходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The investigation has hit a dead end.
exercises.why: **зашло** is the past tense (neuter) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **заходило** is imperfective (**заходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **ушёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **уходил** is imperfective (**уходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **сошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **сойти** (to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сходить**. past: он сошёл · она сошла́ · оно сошло́ · они сошли́. — Wiktionary, «сойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **сходил** is imperfective (**сходить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The conversation lasted until after midnight.
exercises.why: **зашла** is the past tense (feminine) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. exercises.q: Tom unlocked the door and went in.
exercises.why: **вошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **войти** (to enter, to go in(to) (by foot), to get in(to); to penetrate into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **входить**. past: он вошёл · она вошла́ · оно вошло́ · они вошли́. — Wiktionary, «войти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Compare: «Я вошёл в комнату и открыл окно.» (Perfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Я войду в комнату и открою окно.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  The other choice: **входил** is imperfective (**входить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **влез** is the past tense (masculine) of **влезть** (to get into (something, also figurative), to climb into, to scramble into; to fit in, to go in) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **влезать**. past: он вле́з · она вле́зла · оно вле́зло · они вле́зли. — Wiktionary, «влезть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **влезал** is imperfective (**влезать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The gazelle ran away from the cheetah.
exercises.why: **убежала** is the past tense (feminine) of **убежать** (to run away, to make off, to flee; to escape) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **убегать**. past: он убежа́л · она убежа́ла · оно убежа́ло · они убежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «убежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **убегала** is imperfective (**убегать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The moon emerged from behind the cloud.
exercises.why: **выплыла** is the past tense (feminine) of **выплыть** (to swim out (from somewhere)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выплывать**. past: он вы́плыл · она вы́плыла · оно вы́плыло · они вы́плыли. — Wiktionary, «выплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **выплывала** is imperfective (**выплывать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: An explosion blew the house apart.
exercises.why: **разнёс** is the past tense (masculine) of **разнести** (to carry, to convey, to deliver; (colloquial) (news, rumor etc) to spread around) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **разносить**. past: он разнёс · она разнесла́ · оно разнесло́ · они разнесли́. — Wiktionary, «разнести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **разносил** is imperfective (**разносить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **улетал** is imperfective (**улетать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Motion verbs combine with prefixes to form new aspectual pairs, which lose the distinction of directionality, but gain spatial or temporal meanings. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The moon rose above the clouds.
exercises.why: **выплыла** is the past tense (feminine) of **выплыть** (to swim out (from somewhere)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выплывать**. past: он вы́плыл · она вы́плыла · оно вы́плыло · они вы́плыли. — Wiktionary, «выплыть» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **выплывала** is imperfective (**выплывать**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **ввели** is the past tense (plural) of **ввести** (to introduce; to bring in, to usher in) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вводить**. past: он ввёл · она ввела́ · оно ввело́ · они ввели́. — Wiktionary, «ввести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Any prefix (except "по-"), added to the imperf. pair of "going verbs" (to both, repeated and actual functions), makes them an ordinary imperfective-perfective pair.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  «The unidirectional verb serves as the base for the perfective, and the multidirectional as the base for the imperfective.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choice: **вводили** is imperfective (**вводить**).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
